instruction: Rename Armature Bones to Restore Skinning `/home/user/Desktop/scene.blend` contains an armature object `Rig` (a 4-bone chain) and a mesh object `Skin` with an Armature modifier bound to `Rig`. The mesh's vertex groups expect bones named `Bone.Root`, `Bone.A`, `Bone.B`, `Bone.Tip` arranged root-to-tip along the chain, but the armature's bones currently carry generic auto-numbered names, so the Armature modifier does not deform the mesh. Rename the bones so the vertex groups resolve against the rig, and save the result to `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend`. ## Requirements 1. `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend` opens as a valid Blender file. 2. An armature object named `Rig` exists (type `ARMATURE`). 3. `Rig`'s armature has exactly 4 bones. 4. The bone names on `Rig` are exactly the set `{Bone.Root, Bone.A, Bone.B, Bone.Tip}`. 5. The parent chain is `Bone.Root` (no parent) → `Bone.A` → `Bone.B` → `Bone.Tip`. 6. A mesh object named `Skin` exists and has an `ARMATURE` modifier whose `object` is `Rig`. 7. `Skin`'s vertex groups are exactly `{Bone.Root, Bone.A, Bone.B, Bone.Tip}`. 8. Every vertex-group name on `Skin` corresponds to a bone that exists on `Rig` (no missing-bone references). Do not add, remove, or reparent bones; only their names should change. [Software] Launch Blender by running `blender` from a terminal.
